newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein holds after fall.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein holds after fall.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were stable in late Thursday trading after early falls, but buyers were only taking small quantities in anticipation of further declines, traders said.
They said olein prices were around 1,400-05 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, but quotes were also heard at 1,390-95 rupiah for small offtakes. Crude palm oil was below 1,200 rupiah/kg in Medan.
"Trades for small quantities were mostly at the lower level of the market range," one trader said.
"Players are also waiting to see if increases in Malaysia today would be sustained," the trader said.
Malaysian prices climbed largely on talk that Pakistan had secured a $10 million financing facility to buy about 20,000 to 30,000 tonnes of vegetable oil.
Traders said local sentiment remained weak in the wake of President Suharto's recent call for market operations in essential commodities to control prices.
They said players also feared an oversupply situation following state-run joint marketing agency KPB's decision to freeze the signing of new export contracts in October.
"There is some uncertainty in the market, and there is potential for prices to go lower," one trader said.
